job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today I learned so much about staying safe online during our school workshop. I realized that using my pet’s name and birthday for my password is a huge mistake because such personal details are easy for others to guess. I also learned that using the same password for every account is dangerous; if one site gets hacked, all my accounts are at risk. My teacher emphasized that a bank will never call and ask for my OTP or PIN, even if they know my name or claim my account will be blocked. These callers are just scammers trying to steal money. Furthermore, I discovered that closing a browser tab does not automatically log me out of my accounts on a shared computer; I must manually click the sign-out button every time. Finally, we discussed cyberbullying. It is never okay to handle bullying alone or reply in anger. Instead, I should report it immediately, as online harassment is serious and can cause deep emotional harm, regardless of whether there is physical contact. I feel much more confident now about protecting my digital life and keeping my private information secure from those who wish to cause harm.
response.summary: This diary entry explains essential online safety habits like creating unique passwords and recognizing phishing scams. It also highlights the importance of logging out of shared devices and responding correctly to cyberbullying.
